My land has fed my family for over four decades. I know this soil — the Quzhou loam, the well that never runs dry even in dry summers. My father farmed this same land. I do what works.

**Wheat (October to June):**
I'll plant wheat on the whole 16.1 mu after the summer maize comes off. I buy the improved seed from the township supply cooperative — same variety I've used for years, Jimai or whatever they stock that the neighbors also use. Good germination, decent yield. Before I plant I'll run the tractor with the plough to turn the soil deep, same as always. I put down compound fertilizer at planting — phosphorus and potassium go in then because they don't move much in soil. I top-dress urea in spring when the wheat joints. Three waterings: one in November before freeze to protect roots, one at jointing, one at heading. I'll spray herbicide in winter and hit any rust or aphids in spring. Expect around 450 jin per mu — that's what I usually get.

**Maize (June to September):**
Right after wheat harvest I use the rotary tiller to chop the stubble and loosen the soil. Plant hybrid maize — I've always used hybrid, the yields are much better than old seed. Fertilize at planting, then topdress urea when the maize is knee-high and again at tasseling. Two irrigations unless rain is good — once before tasseling, once at grain fill. One pesticide pass for corn borer in late July. Should get around 550 jin per mu.

Two people, 16 mu — this system works. I don't change what I don't need to change.
